source.title: Ridgeless Interpolation with Shallow ReLU Networks in $1D$ is Nearest Neighbor Curvature Extrapolation and Provably Generalizes on Lipschitz Functions

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Provides a theoretical, differently measured result about generalization by interpolating shallow networks, but does not test the listed empirical claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper proves generalization bounds for minimum-weight-norm interpolants; it does not train on random labels or compare architectures, optimizers, batch sizes, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proves generalization bounds for minimum-weight-norm interpolants in noiseless one-dimensional Lipschitz regression. These results test none of V1–V8: interpolation alone does not establish random-label versus natural-label behavior, and a width-independent bound does not establish decreasing test error with width.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate with a qualification: the paper characterizes minimum-neuron-weight-norm shallow ReLU interpolants with unregularized biases and an additional unregularized affine term, and proves optimal-order uniform error bounds for noiseless one-dimensional Lipschitz regression. It does not establish that gradient training reaches these interpolants.
record.recipe_differences: The analysis concerns exact interpolation with minimum parameter ℓ2 norm (equivalently, minimum total variation of the derivative in the stated setting); it does not study a standard gradient-training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The stated bounds distinguish uniformly spaced inputs from iid inputs; the iid bound includes a logarithmic factor and holds with high probability.

fits_no_version.finding: Every minimum-neuron-weight-norm shallow ReLU interpolant with an additional unregularized affine term has Lipschitz constant no greater than that of the noiseless target.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For scalar Lipschitz regression, these interpolants preserve the target's Lipschitz bound and have uniform prediction error at most 2L/m on the grid xi=i/m, or order L log(m)/m with high probability under iid uniform sampling.

fits_no_version.finding: Localizing the minimum-total-variation argument gives a weaker bound for the same interpolants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The localized argument bounds uniform-grid prediction error by 14L/m.

record.problems: The paper explicitly does not study optimization or whether gradient descent with a decaying weight-decay penalty converges to the characterized interpolants. Results are theoretical and restricted to one-dimensional Lipschitz regression; the stated interpolation guarantees require sufficient width.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out classification accuracy on random versus natural labels under the same architecture and training recipe.
Whether test error decreases as width increases beyond the width needed for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes to the training recipe.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical results are substantive but fall outside all eight specified versions. Their restricted setting is therefore not grounds for limits_scope verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label experiment, natural-label classification experiment, or standard-gradient training comparison.
No width sweep or test-error comparison across widths.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

rows.operation_detail: Theoretical bound on the Lipschitz constant of minimum-weight-norm interpolants
rows.measure: supremum of the interpolants' Lipschitz constants
rows.note: Uniform guarantee over RidgelessReLU(D), the interpolants with minimal parameter ℓ2 norm; this is a theorem, not a measured training result.
rows.check: The Lipschitz bound is correctly reported but measures none of the listed effects. Equation (1.6) does not require uniformly spaced inputs. The minimized penalty covers neuron weights; neuron biases and the additional affine term are unregularized.
